This satellite image, captured during the summer season in Switzerland, showcases a diverse landscape within the "temperate, no dry season, warm summer" climate zone. The dominant feature is pastures (~461,000 sqm), which are distributed across two areas, one of which is a large expanse (~452,000 sqm) and the other a marginal area covering less than 5% of the total area. Arable land (~376,000 sqm) is the second most prominent and is fragmented into three areas, including one smaller patch (~281,000 sqm) and two marginal ones. The landscape is also characterized by smaller areas of mixed forest (~351,000 sqm), which is divided into two smaller areas (~216,000 sqm and ~135,000 sqm), and broad-leaved forest (~253,000 sqm), which is itself fragmented into three areas, including one smaller patch (~175,000 sqm) and two marginal ones.

The pastures border arable land, mixed forest, and broad-leaved forest. Moreover, arable land is adjacent to both mixed and broad-leaved forests. In addition, mixed forest is next to broad-leaved forest. This complex interplay of agricultural areas, including pastures and arable land, and forest and seminatural areas, highlights a varied and dynamic ecosystem.
